Cc: security@medilabs.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deployment — connectivity & separation details request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is preparing the final SIG/CAIQ review for the private deployment and we have a handful of follow-ups specific to network separation and residency. Would you be able to provide a short technical packet that covers the items below? A single zip or a Drive link is fine.

- VPC connectivity options available for Private (VPC peering, PrivateLink, dedicated interconnect) and recommended mode for EU-hosted tenants.
- How tenant separation is enforced at the network layer (NSGs, security groups, separate VPCs per tenant?).
- Egress controls: fixed IP ranges (if any), NAT architecture, and support for customer-managed proxy.
- KMS key locality for encryption-at-rest and whether CMKs can be constrained to EU regions.
- Audit/logging evidence: sampling of access logs, retention windows, and where logs are stored (region).
- Any SOC 2 / CAIQ / SIG artifacts you can share or links to summary pages.

We'd like to review this and then schedule a 30-min call to clarify a couple of items. Can you turn this around by EOD Wednesday (21st)?

Best,
Tom Rivers
Security Manager, MediLabs
security@medilabs.com

[Attachment: request-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@medilabs.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — connectivity & separation details request

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a compact packet that addresses each bullet and include a diagram and the SIG/CAIQ pointers. Quick answers to set expectations:

- Recommended connectivity: PrivateLink for minimal blast radius; VPC peering available for high-throughput scenarios. We'll document tradeoffs.
- Tenant separation: by default isolated VPC per customer in EU Private; we can discuss per-tenant NSG overlays if you need extra segmentation.
- Egress: we can provide maintained egress IP ranges for customers who need allow-listing; NAT is handled per-VPC and can be fronted by a customer-managed proxy.
- KMS: CMKs can be constrained to an EU region and we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key).
- Audit/logs: we will include sample ELK/CloudLogging paths and retention defaults (90 days default, options to extend).

I attached an initial summary and a connection diagram. If you can confirm the specific EU region (e.g., eu-west-1) you plan to target, we'll make the egress IP table region-specific.

I'll loop in Rishi and Irene to pull the technical artifacts. We should be able to deliver by EOD Wednesday as requested.

Attachments: redwood-sig-residency-summary.pdf, vpc-connection-diagram.png

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / team —

Draft packet items attached and quick answers inline below. Will update the Drive packet after your review.

- Egress IPs: attached egress-ip-list.csv (these are the maintained NAT egress ranges for eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). If MediLabs needs a static single IP, we recommend fronting with a customer-managed proxy / static NAT appliance.
- NAT architecture: per-VPC NAT gateway by default; we support consolidating NATs into shared transit for cost-savings.
- Tenant separation: we deploy isolated VPCs per customer in Private mode and enforce ACLs + security group baseline via our deployment templates. No shared tenant subnets in Private.
- KMS: see kms-partitioning-notes.txt — CMKs can be created in the customer's EU region; RBAC and key policies can be scoped by tenant ID. We do not export keys out of-region.
- Audit/logs: sample paths and a redacted access log snippet included in the Drive link; retention default 90 days, longer available via subscription.

Attachments added: egress-ip-list.csv, kms-partitioning-notes.txt, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf
